_: Host descriptors for scripts/pack-host.mjs. Governed by docs/design/ADR-0008-host-packaging-seam.md. Data only: adding a host is a new entry in `hosts`, not a change to the packer. Every `why` is the clause that authorises the rule — a rule without one is a rule nobody reviewed.
verificationNote: Historical descriptor review: vendor docs and community write-ups on 2 Aug 2026, not installed-host tests. Row-specific dates/scopes supersede that observation where present. Reconfirm each host before claiming working discovery or execution.

launch._: ADR-0008 D8.7 — one launch contract, three emitters. {{REPO}} resolves to the absolute repo path at pack time because no target host expands ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}. Kept as one field so a runtime change stays a one-line edit here instead of a change to two JSON emitters and a TOML one.

heldBackSkills.why: ADR-0008 C2 — its subject is Claude Code's Workflow tool; remove the tool and nothing remains.
ADR-0008 C2 — its subject is .claude/settings.json, Claude Code hooks and permissions.
ADR-0008 C2 — its deliverable is a skill that passes this repo's scripts/validate.mjs.
ADR-0008 C2 — deployment is Claude Code Routines / /loop / headless runs.

excludeGlobs.why: ADR-0008 D8.6 — all 28 target the Workflow tool. Dead weight and an implicit promise the host cannot keep.

stubFiles.why: ADR-0008 D8.6 — routes between Claude model tiers; wrong advice on a host running Gemini or GPT. Stubbed rather than deleted so the router's pointer does not dangle.

carryFiles.why: ADR-0008 D8.9 class 1 — the autonomy ladder has exactly one definitional home and it lives inside a held-back skill. proof-operate points at it four times and defines its central concept by that pointer. Carried without proof-autopilot's SKILL.md, so the host sees an appendix, not a skill.
ADR-0008 D8.9 class 3 — proof-orchestrate's planning layer constrains a plan against this policy. The constraint survives without the executor.
ADR-0008 D8.9 class 3 — same: loop shape and barrier discipline are planning doctrine, readable without the tool that runs them.

ADR-0008 D8.9 class 2 — 13 packed skills point here for the --mode dial. The file itself routes between Claude model tiers (D8.6), so it is stubbed in place: the pointer resolves and the reader is told why the contract is absent, instead of being handed routing advice for models this host does not run.

dropSections.heading: ### 9. Handoff for authorized execution
dropSections.why: ADR-0008 D8.5 — an execution clause that cannot be made true by renaming a noun. The planning the skill exists for is untouched.

dropSections.heading: ## Orchestration
dropSections.why: ADR-0008 D8.5 — same: names the conductor template this pack does not ship.

rewrites.why: Host verification capability in proof-test and proof-debug; availability is checked by the surrounding instruction.

rewrites.replace: your host's own browser control, if it has one

stripArgumentHintFlags.why: ADR-0008 D8.5 — `argument-hint` is the one line of a skill a host renders as a promise about its own invocation. Every bracketed flag (`--mode`, `--planner`, `--fable-gate`, `--budget`, `--dry-run`) is parsed by proof-engine, which is not in the pack, so advertising them is a false promise. The positional argument is kept; everything from the first ` [` is dropped.
stripArgumentHintFlags.appliesTo: the argument-hint line of a packed SKILL.md, nowhere else

banner: > **Host note — generated pack for {{HOST_NAME}}, do not edit.**
> This copy is generated from `.claude/skills/` in [Proof](https://github.com/santapong/Proof);
> edit it there. This pack does not supply Claude Code's Workflow runtime. This skill's
> `templates/*.workflow.js` orchestration script is **not included** and the Workflow run it
> describes is unavailable here. Work the phases sequentially in one session, in the order given,
> keeping every gate — the judgment is unchanged, only the fan-out is gone. The multi-agent
> version targets Claude Code with the required Workflow capability and permissions.
stubBody: This file exists in the Proof source tree but is **excluded from the {{HOST_NAME}} pack**.
It is stubbed rather than deleted so that pointers to it resolve and you are told why, instead
of following a dead link or reading advice that does not hold on this host.
carriedNotice: > **Carried into this pack without its skill.** The `{{SKILL}}` router is held back on
> {{HOST_NAME}} (ADR-0008 §C2), but this reference file is carried because packed skills define
> terms by pointing at it. Read it as an appendix: {{WHY}}

cursor.note: Cursor also loads .claude/skills/, .codex/skills/ and .agents/skills/ for compatibility. A user who has already cloned Proof can point Cursor at the checkout instead of installing this pack — but never generate a pack INTO one of those paths inside this repo (ADR-0008 C3: a Cursor session would load all 22 skills three times).
cursor.friction: ~40 active tools across all servers before tools are silently dropped (Proof ships 5). No MCP hot-reload — reload the window after editing mcp.json.

codex.friction: config.toml is TOML, not JSON, and the table is [mcp_servers.<name>] — the one config dialect that genuinely differs. `codex mcp add` is safer than hand-editing; the emitted fragment is for review or append.
codex.verificationScope: Current official skill paths reviewed; generated package and local tool probe only, not an authenticated Codex model/skill session

antigravity.note: ~/.gemini/config/skills/ is the only path all three Antigravity variants (AGY, IDE, CLI) read. Installing to a variant-specific path is the most likely 'it silently did nothing' failure.
antigravity.friction: Also readable at ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json or workspace .agents/mcp_config.json. Remote (HTTP) servers use `serverUrl`, not `url` — irrelevant for our stdio server today, and a trap the day HTTP transport un-defers.
